work_package: WP5 -- audit anchor promotions and the full strict core (Glossa Lab repair program, 2026-10-26)

method.strict_core_definition: Anchors with confidence HIGH or MEDIUM in the canonical anchor table whose Phase-108 register category is not SA_DERIVED or SA_CONFIRMED_ONLY and whose register record has sa_in_chain false.
method.ordering: Phase-48 promotions first, in the order recorded in outputs/phase48_medium_validation.json; then the remaining strict-core entries by sign.

phase48_code_facts.fact: test_positional(sign, reading, role) never uses the reading argument: it checks only the Holdat role's average position and starter/ending flags against the role expectation. A positional test that ignores the proposed reading cannot validate that reading; at most it tests distribution and functional role.
test_positional returns (True, 'no_expectation—pass_by_default') when the role has no expectation entry (for example UNKNOWN or a missing role): an uncheckable case is scored as a pass.
test_dedr returns (True, 'too_short_pass') when the reading has fewer than 2 characters after normalization: an uncheckable case is scored as a pass.

Otherwise test_dedr counts dictionary entries equal to the normalized reading (exact match) or sharing its first 3 normalized characters (prefix match, pass at 2 or more). That tests whether a similar word exists in the dictionary -- lexical plausibility -- not whether this sign stood for that word.

test_bigram_consistency returns (True, 'char_not_in_lm—pass_by_default') when the reading's first character is absent from the language model, and (True, 'no_anchor_neighbours—pass_by_default') when none of the sign's top following signs has a HIGH or MEDIUM anchor reading: both uncheckable cases are scored as passes.

The two branches of test_bigram_consistency compute different comparison sets by construction. When torch is importable, the comparison set is the top-5 continuation characters of the reading's character (row.topk(min(5, n))). When torch is absent, the set is every continuation character attested for that character ({b for (a, b) in bigram_prob if a == reading_char}). The CPU form is a superset of the torch form, so the same sign can pass on one backend and fail on the other; the backends do not implement the same method. The recorded Phase-48 run reports gpu_device 'cuda', i.e. the torch branch; a rerun without torch would not be computing the same test.
Promotion required any 2 of the 3 tests to pass (score >= 2), so default credits counted toward promotion exactly like measured passes.

method.no_calibrated_probabilities: This audit records no probability, percentage confidence, or score for any reading. Historical confidence categories are quoted as recorded; current statuses use the fixed vocabulary above.
method.falsifier_rule: A falsifier is reported only where a per-sign falsifier is recorded in the inputs. The generator scans the anchor entry and the register record for a falsifier field; in the audited snapshot there is none for any strict-core entry, so every record states 'no falsifier recorded'.

tier_count_check.resolution: The canonical anchors file itself holds HIGH 166, MEDIUM 5, LOW 3, CANDIDATE 113 (287 entries), and its own by_confidence field agrees. The README errata of 2026-10-12 states the same numbers, so the errata is correct. reports/phase109_rebase.json states LOW 112 and CANDIDATE 4: that file misstates the current canonical table. Its own basis line shows why -- it was computed on the post-Phase-109 table, before Phase-110 demoted 109 Phase-111 'kur' entries from LOW to CANDIDATE (112 - 109 = 3 LOW; 4 + 109 = 113 CANDIDATE; see the _phase110_note field in the anchors file). The rebase file is a superseded snapshot, not an arithmetic error at its own basis date, but any current claim quoting its LOW/CANDIDATE counts is quoting stale numbers.

phase48_summary.note: Strictly, no promotion rests wholly on default credits if the positional pass is counted, because the positional test genuinely measured position for all 30 signs. But the positional test never uses the reading. For the reading itself, the promotions listed under promotions_with_no_reading_sensitive_non_default_pass have no non-default reading-sensitive support at all: every reading-touching pass they received was granted by default.
